blindToFinalChanges.reason: Revealed explicit sensitive-scalp positioning on brand-owner page + 'Ultra Sensitiv' pack front; scalpComfortTarget targeted (7.2 row).
Revealed 'Jeden Tag' in the brand-owner product name; cleansingStrength moderate (not strong) -> Section 9 frequent trigger met.

cleansingStrength.rationale: Moderate: one ether-sulfate primary (SLES #2) buffered by an amphoteric sultaine (#4) and a nonionic glucoside (#6) plus a refatter (#7); no second anionic or reset route. This is exactly the C1 pattern.
counterSignals: SLES is directly after water, so the anionic route is prominent (argues against low).
Three buffering/refatting routes before Panthenol and fragrance-free mild positioning argue toward low.
cleansingStrength.whyNotNeighbor: Low requires an architecture dominated by mild amphoteric/nonionic/amino-acid routes; here SLES is the primary surfactant.

conditioningLevel.rationale: Moderate: one meaningful cationic system (guar HPTC #10) plus light refatting/humectant routes gives noticeable but bounded slip; no silicone, fatty alcohol or pearlizer.
counterSignals: Guar sits after Allantoin at #10, so its level is probably modest.
conditioningLevel.whyNotNeighbor: Low means cleansing-led with little substantive slip; a cationic guar plus a refatter is a real conditioning system.

weightPotential.rationale: Low: the only hair-substantive deposit is one mid-list guar polymer plus a light refatter, delivered in an effective SLES base; noticeable loss of movement or root lift is unlikely.
rules: Section 6 anchors (one light polymer / weak refatter can remain low)
counterSignals: Cationic guar can build up with repeated use on porous (bleached) hair.
weightPotential.whyThisBand: Single light deposition route, no silicone/oil payload, ordinary reset.
weightPotential.whyNotNeighborBand: Moderate needs one meaningfully persistent system or interacting routes; guar at #10 with no silicone does not reach that.

focusPrimary.rationale: scalp_active: the product is explicitly positioned for very sensitive scalp and its formula supports that role (fragrance-free, Allantoin/Panthenol, buffered cleansing).

customerFit.separationNote: User fit (Section 15). Does not change any property above. Cosmetic guidance only.
customerFit.customer: Viola: wavy, fine strands, high density, medium length, coloured + bleached, elastic test snaps, dry scalp without flakes/itch, dry lengths, frizz, tangling, low shine, lost wave shape. Washes ~2x/week, this shampoo ~1x/week; then Syoss Intense Glaze (lamination mask) as conditioner, Neqi leave-in mist, Neqi Opulent Oil.
customerFit.summary: Fine to keep as one of her wash shampoos. It is light (won't flatten fine waves), fragrance-free and comfortable for a dry-feeling scalp. It is not the lever for her dry, frizzy, snapping lengths; those depend on the after-wash care and on how much the bleached lengths get washed.
whyItFits: Low weight: suits fine strands and does not add buildup that would pull waves flat.
Fragrance-free with glycerin, panthenol, allantoin and a refatter: comfortable for a dry-feeling scalp.
Moderate (buffered) cleansing: cleans off the film from the glaze mask, leave-in and oil; that may help her wave shape come back.
watchOuts: Cleansing strength on bleached hair: it is an ordinary sulfate shampoo, not an ultra-mild one. On bleached hair that snaps, wash the scalp and let the foam run through the lengths. Don't scrub the lengths or lather twice.
Its care for the lengths is moderate (one guar conditioner, no silicone), so it doesn't fix dryness, frizz or tangles. The conditioner step has to do that work.

The 'sensitive scalp' label is more than she needs right now; it does no harm. In our candidate projection it would only be matched to the sensitive-scalp group, not to a dry-scalp group, so the app may not suggest it to her.
Possible weight from the rest of her routine (glaze mask + leave-in + oil on fine, dense hair) is a more likely cause of lost wave shape than this shampoo.
swapIf: Her scalp feels tight or itchy after washing, or the lengths feel squeaky or straw-like even after the mask -> try a lower-cleansing (amphoteric/glucoside-based) shampoo for the lengths.
callQuestions: Which shampoo do you use for the other wash each week, and why do you switch between the two?
How do you wash: only the scalp or the lengths too, once or twice, and how does your scalp feel afterwards (tight, comfortable)?
Do you use the Syoss glaze mask every wash instead of a conditioner, and how much oil do you use? Are the waves flatter on the day after the mask?
customerFit.confidence: moderate (no direct observation of her hair; depends on the unknown second shampoo and her technique)
